tool_args.rationale: The five pilot rows show a concave input response at the target horizon, but s_grad spans only 0.018. Over that range, changing sink inhibition mostly rescales the source term, so a close pilot fit would not establish accuracy at wider gradients. The open-branch probe is the lowest-cost targeted way to separate those effects.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit the two-layer siphon with a square-root branch or linear bleed
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: The pilot can constrain the input curve, but the narrow gradient range makes source strength and sink inhibition hard to separate. Fixing inhibition to an archived value would assume it transfers to this system.
It can mimic a sink-modulated curve near s_grad = 1 without predicting how the response changes away from that range.
It costs more and targets temporal dynamics rather than the unresolved sink-gradient dependence.
